free_tier.stated: USD 0 a month with 100 compute minutes per month and up to 1 concurrent virtual machine
free_tier.notes: Compute minutes are consumed with a machine-type multiplier: the Mac M4 Base is 1x, the M4 Pro is 2x and the M4 Max is 4x; only the 4-core 8 GB Base is generally available. The Developer plan is USD 11.99 a month with 1000 compute minutes.

per_object_cap.stated: not an object-storage offer; no per-file size ceiling is published on the pricing or instance pages

retention.stated: not stated on the pricing page; CI runners are provisioned per workflow job and deleted when the job completes, while dashboard VMs persist until stopped

egress.terms: not published: the pricing page states no egress allowance or transfer price; the paid Team plan rate is quoted at USD 0.011 per compute minute against GitHub Hosted at USD 0.062 per minute

interface_detail: a REST API for VM management, an integrated remote terminal and remote display in the dashboard, and SSH access to a virtual machine; GitHub Actions and GitLab CI jobs use a custom runner label
tooling: a GitHub account to install the GetMac GitHub App, or the GetMac dashboard; Golang and Python SDKs are published; a GitHub Actions workflow sets runs-on: getmac
chaining: the free 100 compute minutes a month cover short Xcode and Fastlane CI jobs through a drop-in GitHub Actions runner label, with longer or parallel jobs requiring a paid plan.

limits.value: 100 compute minutes a month on Free; up to 1 concurrent virtual machine; extra usage needs a paid plan
machine type multiplier: Mac M4 Base 4 cores/8 GB at 1x, M4 Pro 2x and M4 Max 4x, the latter two marked Coming Soon
a GetMac account is required; sign-in offers Google, GitHub or an email address

limits_note: The pricing page does not state a job wall-clock cap, an idle reap rule or an egress quota.
binding_note: The 100 compute minutes a month and single concurrent VM limit what a Free account can run before it must move to a paid plan.

identity_cost.detail: the marketing page says no credit card is required; the dashboard sign-in page offers Continue with Google, Continue with GitHub or an Email field with Continue with email. No phone or ID document is requested on that page.

reliability_note: The vendor states a 99.9% uptime SLA on owned Apple Silicon hardware in a TIER III data center; runner jobs use fresh isolated macOS environments. The pricing page does not state a job timeout or idle reap rule.
confidence_note: the pricing page, landing page, documentation index and dashboard sign-in page were read on 2026-11-25; the quoted lines establish the free allowance, concurrent VM cap, no-card statement and signup gate. The sign-in page's public form was read directly; the rung stays documented because no live VM was measured.
